title: Make interrupted jobs retryable and picked up by drain
summary: A job that is dispatched with no live process and no closing record (e.g. after a container restart) is accepted by `athena retry`, and `athena drain` lists it as work and retries it. Audience: the user running athena on machines that can restart, who today must close the job by hand and re-ask.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for retry and drain on interrupted jobs; cargo test, clippy pass.
Criteria run retry and drain on an interrupted job.
Fix retry's state check and drain's selection, not just this job.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Interrupted means JobState::Dispatched with no process in the registry and no closing record.
Retrying an interrupted job leaves the old job unclosed unless the existing flow closes it; the retry proposal carries the original request.
The earlier attempt for an interrupted job may lack verification/outcome records, so the check requiring them must be relaxed for this case.
Drain's queue selection is per channel, as for other retryable jobs.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test (cargo test) makes a job dispatched with no live process, runs retry on it, and gets a proposal whose request is 'try again on <id>' carrying the original request, not the error 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again'.
A test (cargo test) shows a job whose process is still running is refused by retry with a clear message saying it is running.
A drain test (cargo test) with an interrupted job on the drained channel shows it listed as work and retried, with no empty-queue report; an interrupted job on another channel is left alone.
The `athena status` next-step hint for interrupted jobs (status.rs) and the run.rs interrupted message name retry as a way to resume, alongside close.
drain.rs module docs and CHANGELOG.md describe interrupted jobs being retryable and drained.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Changing how running jobs are tracked or supervised
Automatic restart of jobs without drain or retry
Changes to the plan/read state bug in the referenced request
